A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIT research work. Their main text, figures, equations and appendices support comparison, including matching content across renumbering, relocation and redrawing.

before.justification: v1 reports original FIT experiments on SS, SMNLI and BBQ, plus prompt-paraphrasing and SHANS experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds zero-shot, conventional SFT and Product of Experts comparisons.

M1.justification: The focus-instruction set, focus-label rules, training objective and Algorithm 1 retain the same FIT procedure. Revised terminology and mathematical explanations do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SS sentiment classification, SMNLI inference including held-out genres, BBQ with seen and unseen bias features, and SHANS. The added comparisons use existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds zero-shot and conventional ground-truth-label SFT comparisons on SS, SMNLI and BBQ (Figures 7–9), and Product of Experts on BBQ (Figure 11). The original SFT comparator remains, now explicitly identified as SFT(yfocus). These additions substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The new BBQ debiasing experiment introduces a comparison of PoE under default prompts with FIT under focus(C), scoring both against ground-truth answers (A.8). The retained experiments keep their stated splits, co-occurrence rates, model sizes, focus-accuracy metric and decoding settings.

E4.justification: The prompt-paraphrasing analysis is retained, but Llama's same-prompt accuracy curves change between v1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 10 after matching reordered model columns. Its qualitative robustness conclusion remains unchanged. The SHANS results and overlapping-heuristic failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates for the experimental results. Updated accuracy curves do not introduce a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for zero-shot, conventional SFT and PoE comparisons. Existing results also change, including SS FIT curves in Figure 3 and few-shot/SFT curves in SMNLI Figure 4. Figure 11 newly reports comparable task accuracy for PoE and FIT, with FIT retaining greater instruction-dependent steerability. The PDFs do not explain these updates as reruns.

T1.justification: Definition 1 revises predictivity by removing conditioning on the full input. The maximum-entropy argument is replaced with explicit independence conditions and expanded SS/SMNLI propositions and proofs. The SS generating model distinguishes proposed from inserted keywords, and the SMNLI/SHANS label equations change from Y = S to Y = C. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The central claims about steerability, distribution-shift robustness and unseen-feature generalization remain. v2 promotes explainability from a potential application discussed in v1's ethics section to an asserted introductory contribution, and more explicitly frames debiasing as one application of general model control.

C2.justification: New A.2 discusses required knowledge of spurious features, possible automatic feature labeling, and the dataset-curation costs limiting open-ended generation experiments. A.8 adds an interpretation of PoE's two-model requirement and limited steerability. The existing SHANS overlap limitation is preserved.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents balanced-label construction and implementation details for the added baselines, including PoE training on stereotypical labels and normalization of first-output-token logits. Existing LoRA, validation, decoding and prompt-template details largely match. The balancing disclosure alone does not establish a change to previously performed experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the Llama-Guard/JsonTuning comparison with a substantially different positioning around RLHF, safety degradation after fine-tuning, steering vectors and sparse autoencoders. It emphasizes FIT's natural-language adaptability relative to interventions requiring access to representations. Additional references support feature identification, applicability and the PoE comparison.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains intact. v2 makes targeted revisions to the introduction, conclusion and ethics discussion, replaces task-feature terminology from causal to core, rewrites the steering subsection, and separates limitations into A.2 with corresponding appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds three extensive baseline-comparison grids and a PoE comparison figure, redraws the SS generating-process diagram, and resizes or relabels multiple radar charts. It also reorders model columns in the paraphrasing figure, corrects its caption's orientation description, and integrates the previously standalone SHANS plot into its discussion page.

improvement.justification: The conventional SFT(y) controls and PoE comparison strengthen evidence beyond v1's few-shot and focus-label SFT comparisons, while explicit assumptions and limitations improve assessability. Mathematical corrections also help, but new proof errors limit the gain in rigor: Proposition 3 assigns probability 1/2 to the proposed keyword conditional on C, although Equation 14 makes that keyword deterministic given C. Overall, the empirical and documentation gains support a limited quality improvement.
